context: linear · spread moving along the right-of-way: weld → coat → lower → backfill → hydrotest

brief.intro: New to this project type? A cross-country pipeline is built by a 'spread' — a travelling factory of crews that moves along the right-of-way, each crew doing one step and handing the pipe to the next: clear and grade the strip, string the pipes, bend, weld, inspect the welds, coat the joints, dig the trench, lower the pipe in, backfill and restore the land. Progress is counted in welds and kilometres per day. The straight run is routine; the programme is decided by the right-of-way, by special crossings (rivers, highways, railways) done by separate crews, by the stations at each end, and by the hydrostatic test and drying at the finish. Line pipe is ordered months ahead and must be on site before the spread starts.

scope.name: Route survey & right-of-way
scope.desc: Survey, land acquisition and permits for the working strip.

scope.name: Clearing & grading
scope.desc: Preparing a level working strip and access along the route.

scope.name: Stringing & bending
scope.desc: Laying pipes out along the strip and cold-bending them to follow the ground.

scope.name: Mainline welding
scope.desc: Joining pipes into a continuous string, by manual or automatic welding.

scope.name: NDT & joint coating
scope.desc: Radiography or ultrasonic testing of every weld, then coating the joint.

scope.name: Trenching, lowering & backfill
scope.desc: Digging the trench, lowering the welded string, padding and backfilling.

scope.name: Crossings
scope.desc: HDD, boring or open-cut crossings of rivers, roads, railways and other pipelines.

scope.name: Tie-ins
scope.desc: Welding the separately built sections and crossings together.

scope.name: Stations & valves
scope.desc: Block-valve stations, pig launchers / receivers, pump or compressor and metering stations.

scope.name: Cathodic protection & SCADA
scope.desc: Corrosion protection, leak detection and remote control along the line.

scope.name: Hydrotest, drying & commissioning
scope.desc: Cleaning, gauging, pressure test, dewatering, drying and product-in.

must_get_right: Line pipe and its coating are the first critical item; the spread cannot start, and cannot keep moving, without pipe strung ahead of it.
Plan the mainline as a moving sequence with fixed gaps between crews, and count progress in welds per day — one slow crew sets the pace of all.
Schedule each major crossing as its own small project with its own permit, crew and season (river levels); they are done off the main spread and tied in later.
Hydrotest water (source, permit to take and to discharge), test sections and drying are long and easy to forget — especially for gas lines, where drying to dew point takes weeks.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities are organised by spread and by kilometre section, with crossings and stations as separate branches, so welded, lowered, backfilled and tested kilometres can be read at any date.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: The spread works a long-shift calendar; reduced output is assumed in the wet season and in rock or mountain sections. River crossings are tied to low-flow months.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: Per section: ROW → clear and grade → string → weld → NDT → coat → trench → lower → backfill → reinstate, with a set gap between crews. Crossings and stations are built in parallel and joined by tie-ins. Then test sections are cleaned, gauged, hydrotested and dried before product-in. The critical path runs through pipe delivery and the mainline, or through the longest-lead station equipment.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Right-of-way is released ahead of the spread; pipe is delivered to the stringing schedule; test water is available and may be discharged; upstream and downstream facilities are ready for product-in.

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: The spread is long and must keep moving; access is along the ROW only; environmental and seasonal windows apply at rivers, farmland and protected areas.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Main risks: right-of-way delays, rock or wet ground, weld repair rate above plan, a failed crossing (HDD), late valves or rotating equipment, and a failed hydrotest. Contingency is held before the hydrotest and before product-in.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3 by spread and kilometre section; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for each crew of the spread — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
